label: Market
_model: Settlement kernel, but the place is a transaction rather than a community. The appetite belongs to the market itself; the claimants are its offices; and everything it did to people it did by contract, which is why none of it can be undone by force.

appetites.purpose: the trading would never have to stop

appeasement.move: sell something, to anybody, for anything at all

appetites.want: that every dealing here should be exactly fair
appetites.purpose: nobody would ever be wronged in it

appeasement.move: settle one dispute honestly, out loud, against your own interest

appetites.want: never to have a slow day
appetites.purpose: there would always be something moving
appetites.asks: "What will you give me for it?"

appeasement.move: strike a bargain here and shake on it

appetites.want: never to be owed anything by anybody
appetites.purpose: every account would come out clean

appeasement.move: pay something you owe, in full, in front of it

bell.label: the bell that opens the market
bell.function: the only thing that ever started or stopped trading here

standard.label: the standard weight, sealed and true
standard.function: the only measure here that was never adjusted

handsel.label: the first coin of the first day's trading
handsel.function: the only bargain here nobody regretted

bond.label: the bond that was never redeemed
bond.function: the only debt here that was written down honestly

factions.name: the Market
factions.essence: still trading, still crying its wares, still expecting to be dealt with

factions.name: the chapmen
factions.essence: came for the fair and have not managed to leave

factions.name: the Company of Weighers
factions.essence: will not pass anything that does not measure true

factions.name: what got out of the pens
factions.essence: was bought and paid for and never collected

triggerGlossary.announced: came in through the toll gate and paid, as traders do
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: passed the same stall twice without buying
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice in a square built to carry one
triggerGlossary.lingering: stood in one row long enough for the criers to work out what you want
triggerGlossary.disturbed: handled goods, moved a weight, or opened a shuttered booth

foes.name: Bandit
foes.note: cutpurses; they want the purse, not the fight

skirmish.avoid: show them you carry nothing worth taking and they move on

fight.line: 4 Bandits and a Hobgoblin Soldier collecting toll
fight.avoid: they are collecting a toll — pay it and they let you through

foes.name: Necromancer
foes.note: raises one Skeleton per round from the pens

battle.harmedBy: anything — the Necromancer is alive and bleeds
battle.avoid: it stops for a true measure; put the standard weight on the beam and it must check it

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith of the Clerk, 1 Necromancer and 5 Skeletons

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

bargain.dangerLine: everything here still wants to be haggled with, and it will hold you to what you agree

institution: a square laid out in rows, one trade to a row
a court that sits while the dust is still on your feet
stalls numbered and let by the day
ritual: a hand spat on and struck before anything moves
the first coin of the day kept back and not spent
a price cried three times before it is a price
demand: a hand held out, open, waiting to be struck
goods set out with no price on them at all
a stall with the boards down and nobody behind it
wound: a hand struck and then withdrawn, in front of everybody
a row of stalls with the goods still on them and no sellers
a price cried a fourth time, into silence
anchor: the first coin of the first day's trading
a book of bargains struck and honoured
a stall let in perpetuity to somebody who never came

features: a hand held open, waiting
goods set out with no price on them
a first coin kept back on a string
a price cried into an empty row
boards down on an empty stall
a book of bargains left open

decisions.cue: a hand held out open, waiting to be struck
decisions.cost: striking it makes the bargain, whatever it was

resolve.success: you settle the terms before you strike, and the market honours them exactly
resolve.failure: you strike first and find out the terms after: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: do not take the hand; the row closes to you and stays closed

decisions.cue: goods set out with no price on them at all
decisions.cost: naming a price is an offer you are held to

resolve.success: you price it fairly and the Market deals with you as a trader from here on
resolve.failure: you price it low and the seller accepts, and expects the difference
resolve.orElse: offer nothing; you go through the market as a customer, and are treated as prey

decisions.cue: the first coin of the day kept back on a string
decisions.cost: spending it opens the day; keeping it does not

resolve.success: you spend the handsel properly and the whole square begins trading around you
resolve.failure: you pocket it and nothing here will deal with you again
resolve.orElse: leave it hanging; the day never starts and the square stays dead

decisions.cue: a price being cried three times into an empty row
decisions.cost: answering the third cry closes the sale

resolve.success: you answer and get the thing, and the crier owes you a hearing
resolve.failure: you answer late and the sale goes to somebody you cannot see
resolve.orElse: let it lapse; whatever it was is gone for good

decisions.cue: a book of bargains struck and honoured, with a blank line ruled
decisions.cost: entering a bargain in it makes it binding on both

resolve.success: you write terms that bind the Market as much as you and it must keep them
resolve.failure: you write loosely and it keeps the letter of what you wrote: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the line blank; nothing here is bound to you at all

decisions.cue: a stall let in perpetuity to somebody who never came
decisions.cost: standing behind it takes the lease

resolve.success: you take the stall and have standing in the market — the Court will hear you
resolve.failure: you take it and cannot leave it while the market is open
resolve.orElse: walk past; you have no standing and the Court will not sit for you

situations.doing: calling a price three times into an empty row
situations.onArrival: it pauses on the third cry and looks at you
situations.because: the lot must be sold and nobody has bid
situations.offer: bid anything and it will cry your business through the whole square

situations.doing: holding a bargain half-struck between them
situations.onArrival: both hands are open and neither will close
situations.because: the terms were never agreed and neither will speak first
situations.offer: name the terms and both will thank you, and owe you

situations.doing: laying goods out on a stall that already has goods on it
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you are the one who has the pitch
situations.because: they arrived for the fair and the fair was already over
situations.offer: help them clear the pitch and they will tell you what sells here now

situations.doing: holding a purse open with nothing in it
situations.onArrival: it asks what you have brought to sell
situations.because: the fair cannot be declared over while anything is unsold
situations.offer: sell it anything at all and it will declare you under its protection

situations.doing: standing with the boards down and the goods laid out
situations.onArrival: the goods are arranged fresh and the dust is off them
situations.because: the stall is let in perpetuity and the tenant never came
situations.offer: stand behind it and the market treats you as one of its own

situations.doing: weighing a purse against a ledger, over and over
situations.onArrival: one of them slides the purse toward you
situations.because: the account will not come out and they cannot stop trying
situations.offer: balance it for them and they will open the counting house

temptations.cue: the first coin of the first day
temptations.benefit: once, make a deal go through that should not have
temptations.standingDrawback: the market's luck goes with it and the square knows

temptations.benefit: hold anyone here to what they agreed
temptations.standingDrawback: you are in the book too

temptations.benefit: standing in the market, and the Court will hear you
temptations.standingDrawback: you owe the day's rent, and it accrues

temptations.benefit: once, be heard by everything in the square
temptations.standingDrawback: everything in the square then knows where you are

temptations.cue: a purse that is never quite empty
temptations.benefit: once, pay what is asked
temptations.standingDrawback: the coin comes from somebody, and they notice

weights.dangerLine: the Company is still checking, and nothing you carry will pass

institution: a weigh-house on the square with the beam in full view
every measure in the market stamped and sealed once a year
a company whose only work is checking other people's scales
ritual: a beam swung empty each morning to prove it hangs true
seals cut off and restruck at the same hour
the standard brought out, shown, and locked away again
demand: a beam hanging with one pan lower than the other
a measure set out beside a thing that has not been measured
a seal pressed into wax that has not set
wound: a weigh-house with the beam bent and left bent
seals struck onto measures that were never checked
the standard gone from its case and the case still locked
anchor: the standard weight, sealed and true
a book of seals and what they were struck on
a beam that has never been out of true

features: a beam hanging with one pan low
a seal in wax that has not set
a measure set beside something unmeasured
a bent beam left bent
a case locked and empty
a book of seals open at a page

decisions.cue: a beam hanging with one pan lower than the other and nothing in either
decisions.cost: balancing it is a claim about the world

resolve.success: you find the fault and true the beam, and the Company will vouch for you anywhere here
resolve.failure: you weight the light pan to fake it and the Company finds out: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it hanging false; every measure you are given here is short

decisions.cue: a seal pressed into wax that has not set
decisions.cost: the seal can still be lifted or spoiled

resolve.success: you lift it clean and can reseal something the Company will not question
resolve.failure: you smear it and whatever it sealed is now unsealed and known to be
resolve.orElse: let it set; it seals something against you

decisions.cue: a measure set out beside a thing that has not been measured
decisions.cost: measuring it settles what it is worth

resolve.success: you measure honestly and the market prices everything for you at true value
resolve.failure: you measure short in your own favour and the beam remembers
resolve.orElse: take it unmeasured; you will be charged whatever they like

decisions.cue: a locked case with the standard weight gone out of it
decisions.cost: the case says who had the key last

resolve.success: you read the case and learn who took the standard, and where they went with it
resolve.failure: you force the case and the Company treats you as the thief: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it locked; nothing here can be proved true or false

decisions.cue: a book of seals listing what each was struck on
decisions.cost: one entry does not match the goods it sealed

resolve.success: you find the false entry and can hold the Clerk to it
resolve.failure: you are found reading it by something that struck those seals
resolve.orElse: close the book; the false measures stay in circulation, including yours

decisions.cue: a bent beam left bent in a weigh-house that is otherwise kept
decisions.cost: straightening it undoes a great many old bargains

resolve.success: you straighten it and every dishonest thing in the market is exposed at once
resolve.failure: it snaps, and the market has no measure at all: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it bent; the Company will not pass anything you carry

situations.doing: swinging an empty beam to prove it hangs true
situations.onArrival: it stops the beam and offers you the pans
situations.because: the beam is proved each morning and the morning has not ended
situations.offer: put something in a pan and it will weigh anything else you ask

situations.doing: holding a locked case and turning it over
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you have seen the weight
situations.because: the standard was taken and the case never opened since
situations.offer: tell it where the standard is and it will unseal any door here

situations.doing: checking a measure against another measure, endlessly
situations.onArrival: they hand you a third and wait
situations.because: neither will serve as the standard and both know it
situations.offer: give them a true measure and they will pass anything you carry

situations.doing: filing at a weight, carefully, in a doorway
situations.onArrival: they stop and grin rather than hide it
situations.because: nobody has checked anything here in a long time
situations.offer: let them finish and they will file you a weight that passes anywhere

situations.doing: hanging with one pan lower and nothing in either
situations.onArrival: it swings level as you come near and then tips again
situations.because: it was bent once and nobody trued it
situations.offer: true it and the Company vouches for you across the whole market

situations.doing: stamping seals onto measures without checking them
situations.onArrival: it holds a seal out to you, ready struck
situations.because: the sealing must be done and the checking cannot be
situations.offer: refuse the seal and it will tell you which measures are false

temptations.benefit: once, settle any dispute about what is true
temptations.standingDrawback: nothing else here measures true while you hold it

temptations.benefit: once, make a thing pass as sound
temptations.standingDrawback: the Company checks everything you have sealed, eventually

temptations.benefit: know when you are being cheated
temptations.standingDrawback: you know exactly how badly, which is worse

temptations.benefit: once, buy at your own price
temptations.standingDrawback: the beam it was used on stays wrong

temptations.benefit: know which of anything here is false
temptations.standingDrawback: so does whoever notices you reading it

crowd.dangerLine: the market is full and there is nobody in it

institution: a square built to hold four thousand people
rows wide enough for carts and worn narrow by feet
a cross where the crowd is supposed to gather
ritual: a bell rung to open the trading and rung again to close it
the same rows filled in the same order every day
a crowd moving one way round the square and never the other
demand: a gap in the press, exactly one person wide
a cross with the steps worn and nobody on them
a row that stays empty while every other row fills
wound: a square emptied in an afternoon and the goods left standing
a bell rung to close and never rung to open
boots and baskets trodden into the mud in one direction
anchor: the bell that opens the market
a plan of the square with every pitch marked
a crowd that has never once dispersed

features: a gap in a press of nobody
baskets trodden into the mud
a bell rope hanging still
an empty row between full ones
worn steps at a market cross
goods left standing on a pitch

decisions.cue: a bell rung to close the market and never rung to open it
decisions.cost: ringing it starts everything again

resolve.success: you ring the market open and the square fills, and the crowd carries you where you ask
resolve.failure: you ring it and cannot stop it ringing: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the rope; the square stays shut and so does everything in it

decisions.cue: a gap in the press exactly one person wide
decisions.cost: stepping into it joins the crowd

resolve.success: you step in and move through the market unseen, as one of the crowd
resolve.failure: you step in and cannot step out until the crowd does
resolve.orElse: push through instead; you are seen doing it, by everything

decisions.cue: a row that stays empty while every other row fills
decisions.cost: there is a reason nobody stands in it

resolve.success: you learn why the row is avoided and can use it to cross the square safely
resolve.failure: you go down it in ignorance and something in it takes an interest
resolve.orElse: go round the long way, costing a Turn

decisions.cue: a market cross with the steps worn and nobody on them
decisions.cost: the steps are for whoever will be listened to

resolve.success: you speak from the cross and the whole market attends you, once
resolve.failure: you are shouted down and cried through the square as a fool: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stay off the steps; nothing here will hear you out

decisions.cue: baskets and boots trodden into the mud, all pointing one way
decisions.cost: the direction says where everybody went

resolve.success: you follow the direction and find where the square emptied to
resolve.failure: you follow it into the press and are carried the wrong way entirely
resolve.orElse: ignore the mud; you will not know where the crowd went

decisions.cue: a plan of the square with every pitch marked and one crossed out
decisions.cost: the crossed pitch is still let to somebody

resolve.success: you find the crossed pitch and what is still standing on it
resolve.failure: you stand on it and the crowd forms around you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the plan; you will walk onto it by accident later

situations.doing: standing shoulder to shoulder in an empty square
situations.onArrival: it parts, exactly one person wide, in front of you
situations.because: the market is open and the crowd has never dispersed
situations.offer: walk the gap and the crowd will carry you anywhere in the square

situations.doing: holding a rope that is not moving
situations.onArrival: it asks whether it is time yet
situations.because: the market was closed and never opened
situations.offer: tell it to ring and the square comes to life around you

situations.doing: singing to nobody in a full row
situations.onArrival: they break off and ask if you know the second verse
situations.because: they will not stop until somebody buys a sheet
situations.offer: buy a sheet and they will sing you the truth of what happened here

situations.doing: standing on the cross steps with its mouth open
situations.onArrival: no sound comes out and the crowd waits anyway
situations.because: it was crying something when the square emptied
situations.offer: give it words and the whole market will do what you say, once

situations.doing: moving one way around the square, endlessly
situations.onArrival: it slows where you stand and does not stop
situations.because: the crowd goes round this way and always has
situations.offer: go with it once round and every stall opens to you

situations.doing: holding a basket of something nobody bought
situations.onArrival: it holds the basket up without speaking
situations.because: it was sent out to sell and nobody came
situations.offer: buy the basket and it will show you the row nobody uses

temptations.benefit: once, gather or scatter everything in earshot
temptations.standingDrawback: the market opens when you ring it, and does not close

temptations.benefit: know every pitch and who holds it
temptations.standingDrawback: you are marked on it now

temptations.benefit: once, have exactly the small thing you need
temptations.standingDrawback: it was somebody's stock and they want it back

temptations.cue: a ballad sheet about this place
temptations.benefit: know one true thing about what happened here
temptations.standingDrawback: the ballad names you in the last verse

temptations.cue: a chapman's cloak off a peg
temptations.benefit: once, be taken for part of the crowd
temptations.standingDrawback: the crowd expects you to move with it

credit.dangerLine: the market keeps accounts, and yours is open

institution: a counting house with a window onto the square
tally sticks split and matched, one half to each party
a court that can distrain on goods before the dust settles
ritual: accounts read out loud at quarter-day
a tally split in front of witnesses
a debt cried in the square before it is enforced
demand: a tally stick with only one half present
an account ruled off and left unsigned
a hand held out for a payment nobody has named
wound: a strong room with the boxes open and the tallies burnt
a debtors' yard with the gate off its hinges
accounts ruled off in the middle of a quarter
anchor: the bond that was never redeemed
a full set of tallies, both halves

features: a tally stick with one half missing
an account ruled off unsigned
a hand held out for payment
burnt tallies in a grate
a strong-room box standing open
a bond with the seal intact

decisions.cue: a tally stick with only one half present
decisions.cost: the other half is somewhere and matching them settles the debt

resolve.success: you find the matching half at {priorCue} and the debt is discharged in your favour
resolve.failure: you match it wrongly and the debt is now yours: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it unmatched; the Market treats the whole sum as outstanding against you

decisions.cue: an account ruled off and left unsigned
decisions.cost: signing it closes the account for good

resolve.success: you sign it correctly and one thing here stops pursuing you, permanently
resolve.failure: you sign without reading and take on what it says: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it open; the account keeps running and the total keeps growing

decisions.cue: a hand held out for a payment nobody has named
decisions.cost: paying settles something; asking what for does not

resolve.success: you make it name the debt first, and it is smaller than you feared
resolve.failure: you pay blind and have settled somebody else's account, not yours
resolve.orElse: refuse the hand; whatever it was owed is now owed by you

decisions.cue: a strong room with the boxes open and the tallies burnt
decisions.cost: somebody destroyed the record rather than pay

resolve.success: you find whose tallies were burnt and can hold the Clerk to the theft
resolve.failure: you are found in the strong room with burnt tallies in your hand
resolve.orElse: leave it; nobody here can prove anything, including you

decisions.cue: a debtors' yard with the gate off its hinges
decisions.cost: what was held here got out, or was let out

resolve.success: you work out which and can bargain with what is loose in the market
resolve.failure: you go in and the gate is back on its hinges behind you
resolve.orElse: stay out of the yard; something in the market is owed and unaccounted for

decisions.cue: a bond with the seal still intact, unredeemed
decisions.cost: redeeming it ends the debt; breaking the seal voids it

resolve.success: you redeem it properly and the Market considers the whole affair closed
resolve.failure: you break the seal and every debt it stood against comes due at once
resolve.orElse: leave it sealed; the bond is the ending's whole leverage and you will not have it

situations.doing: holding out half a tally stick
situations.onArrival: it does not speak; it waits for the other half
situations.because: the account cannot be closed with one half missing
situations.offer: give it any matching half and it will discharge one debt of yours

situations.doing: sitting in a yard with the gate off its hinges
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you have come to collect
situations.because: they were distrained on and nobody came back
situations.offer: tell them the debt is settled and they will show you what is in the strong room

situations.doing: sitting with an account book open at a ruled line
situations.onArrival: it turns the book toward you and offers a pen
situations.because: the account must be signed off and there is nobody to sign
situations.offer: sign it and the Court will find for you in anything, once

situations.doing: passing a purse back and forth without opening it
situations.onArrival: they stop and hold it out to you
situations.because: neither will accept it and neither will keep it
situations.offer: take the purse and both will owe you, and pay

situations.doing: lying sealed on an empty table in a locked room
situations.onArrival: the seal is unbroken and the wax is still soft
situations.because: it was never redeemed and never destroyed
situations.offer: redeem it and the whole market considers its accounts closed

situations.doing: reading an account aloud to an empty square
situations.onArrival: it reaches your name in the list and stops
situations.because: the quarter's accounts must be cried before they are enforced
situations.offer: let it finish and it will strike your name off with its own hand

temptations.benefit: once, call in a debt from anything here
temptations.standingDrawback: the Market opens an account against you at the same moment

temptations.benefit: prove any debt here settled or outstanding
temptations.standingDrawback: tallies work both ways and yours is one of them

temptations.cue: a distrained purse from the strong room
temptations.benefit: spend freely, once
temptations.standingDrawback: it was distrained off somebody who is still owed it

temptations.benefit: know what everything here owes and to whom
temptations.standingDrawback: you know your own line, and it grows

temptations.cue: the pin off the debtors' gate
temptations.benefit: once, hold something where it is
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever was in the yard is not, and knows you have the pin
